title: The dynamics of functional connectivity-based language lateralization across timescales
title_zh: 基于功能连接的语言侧化在不同时间尺度上的动态变化
abstract: In most individuals, language is predominantly left-lateralized, a prominent feature of human brain organization. Recent research increasingly views language lateralization as a property of distributed and interacting functional networks. In this article, we review evidence that the lateralization of functional connectivity within the language system varies in both degree and direction across multiple timescales. We propose that this connectivity-based lateralization undergoes long-term developmental, experience-dependent, and perturbation-induced reorganization, while also exhibiting short-term context-driven and spontaneous fluctuations within apparently stable patterns. Furthermore, we discuss neurobiological mechanisms that may support and constrain these dynamics. Together, these findings provide a multiscale framework for understanding how the human brain balances functional flexibility with relative stability in shaping the lateralized organization of language.
abstract_zh: 在大多数个体中，语言功能主要呈左侧化，这是人类大脑组织的显著特征。近年来，研究越来越将语言侧化视为分布式且相互作用的功能网络的属性。本文综述了证据，表明语言系统内功能连接的侧化在多个时间尺度上既有程度差异，也有方向变化。我们提出，这种基于连接的侧化经历长期的发育、经验依赖和扰动诱导的重组，同时在表面上稳定的模式中表现出短期的情境驱动和自发波动。此外，我们讨论了可能支持和限制这些动态的神经生物学机制。综上所述，这些发现为理解人类大脑如何在功能灵活性与相对稳定性之间平衡，形成语言侧化组织提供了多尺度框架。
